action: General advice: Workday customers should confirm that payroll runs, time entries and scheduled integrations from the evening of November 13 completed correctly.
exec: A payroll and HR supplier outage reportedly tied to backup-system testing; a reminder to have a fallback for time-critical pay runs.
plain: An outage on the evening of November 13 stopped many employees from signing in to Workday's payroll and staff-management service. Reports tie it to a backup-testing problem; Workday says it was not a cyber incident.
summary: A service disruption on the evening of November 13 locked users out of Workday's payroll and HR platform; Downdetector showed nearly 3,000 outage reports shortly after 5 p.m., FOX Los Angeles reports. The San Francisco Chronicle reported a problem found while testing backup systems. A Workday spokesperson told ABC10, as relayed by UC Today, that the disruption was not related to a cybersecurity incident and service was restored by 11 a.m. EST Saturday.

evidence.quote: The website Downdetector first reported nearly 3,000 outage reports for the platform shortly after 5 p.m. Friday.

title: Workday outage locks employees out of payroll and HR systems

validation.note: Follow-up 22 Nov: FOX 11 Los Angeles (13 Nov; Workday statement to LiveNOW from FOX, nearly 3,000 Downdetector reports, cause per SF Chronicle) and UC Today (14 Nov; Workday spokesperson to ABC10: not related to a cybersecurity incident, restored by 11 a.m. EST Saturday) independently report the outage; HollywoodLife kept. ABC10 not read directly.
